review.summary: The sign face is intact, but the reverse includes two long rows of jagged repeated spikes/fragments around oversized mounting rails. These are not coherent hardware and visibly damage the top/back silhouette.

issues.problem: Invented repeated jagged tabs and fragmented-looking rear detail rather than clean bracket construction.

review.summary: Second sign again invents large repeated rear hardware, now a row of hollow nozzle-like cylinders and tangled small parts behind the otherwise clean sign face.

issues.problem: Large repeated tubes and malformed mechanical details are not coherent road-sign backing.

review.summary: Reduced sign retains clean blank green face/border, rounded slab and coherent rear mounting frame. Five-view source comparison preserves material boundaries and silhouette; fresh FBX/GLB pass at 14,313 triangles.

issues.problem: Small fastener/edge softening, deeper inferred rear frame and rear painted strips remain.

review.summary: Sign face remains blank green with a clean continuous pale border, and rear mounting rails read as metal. No invented lettering or major color bleed.

issues.problem: Inferred narrow vertical rear strips, darker green face and brighter metal highlights differ from the single front reference.

review.summary: Third sign has a clean rounded rectangular plate and coherent rear rails/brackets without the repeated spikes or tubes from the prior attempts. Five views retain the flat sign face and open mounting gap.

issues.problem: Inferred full-width rear mounting rails are deeper/more extensive than the two brackets visible in the reference.
